import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react";
import type { IApiClient } from "@/lib/__shared__/apiClient";

type RequestResponse<T> = [T | null, Error | null];
type CheckoutSessionStatus = "open" | "complete" | null;

export const PLAN_IDS = {
    PREMIUM_MONTHLY: "PREMIUM_MONTHLY",
    PREMIUM_YEARLY: "PREMIUM_YEARLY",
    PLUS_MONTHLY: "PLUS_MONTHLY",
    PLUS_YEARLY: "PLUS_YEARLY",
    LIFETIME: "LIFETIME",
} as const;

export interface AvailablePlans {
    freePlan: {
        name: string;
        description: string;
        features: string[];
    };
    subscriptionPlans: {
        name: string;
        description: string;
        features: string[];
        planTier: "PREMIUM" | "PLUS";
        monthlyVariation: {
            planId: keyof typeof PLAN_IDS;
            totalPrice: number;
            monthlyPrice: number;
            interval: "MONTH";
        };
        yearlyVariation: {
            planId: keyof typeof PLAN_IDS;
            totalPrice: number;
            monthlyPrice: number;
            interval: "YEAR";
        };
    }[];
    lifetimePlan: {
        name: string;
        description: string;
        features: string[];
        planId: keyof typeof PLAN_IDS;
        totalPrice: number;
    };
}

const API_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_USER_SERVER_URL;

export class PaymentManager {
    private apiClient: IApiClient;

    constructor(apiClient: IApiClient) {
        this.apiClient = apiClient;
    }

    async createCheckoutSession(
        planId: keyof typeof PLAN_IDS,
    ): Promise<RequestResponse<{ clientSecret: string }>> {
        try {
            const response = await this.apiClient.fetch(
                `${API_BASE}/payment/create-checkout-session`,
                {
                    method: "POST",
                    body: JSON.stringify({ planId }),
                },
            );

            const json: { data: { clientSecret: string }; message: string } =
                await response.json();

            if (response.ok) {
                return [json.data, null];
            }

            throw new Error(json.message);
        } catch (err) {
            console.error(`Error: ${err}`);
            Sentry.captureException(err);
            return [null, err as Error];
        }
    }

    async getAvailablePlans(): Promise<AvailablePlans> {
        try {
            const response = await this.apiClient.fetch(
                `${API_BASE}/payment/available-plans`,
                {
                    method: "GET",
                },
            );
            const json: { data: AvailablePlans; message: string } =
                await response.json();

            if (response.ok) {
                return json.data;
            }

            throw new Error(json.message);
        } catch (err) {
            console.error(`Error: ${err}`);
            Sentry.captureException(err);
            throw err;
        }
    }

    async getCheckoutSession(sessionId: string): Promise<
        RequestResponse<{
            id: string;
            startDate: string;
            endDate: string;
            publishedPriceUsd: number | null;
            status: CheckoutSessionStatus;
            interval: string;
            planTier: string;
            customerEmail: string;
        }>
    > {
        try {
            const response = await this.apiClient.fetch(
                `${API_BASE}/payment/checkout-session?sessionId=${encodeURIComponent(sessionId)}`,
                {
                    method: "GET",
                },
            );

            const json: {
                data: {
                    status: CheckoutSessionStatus;
                    customerEmail: string;
                    id: string;
                    startDate: string;
                    endDate: string;
                    publishedPriceUsd: number | null;
                    interval: string;
                    planTier: string;
                };
                message: string;
            } = await response.json();

            if (response.ok) {
                return [json.data, null];
            }

            throw new Error(json.message);
        } catch (err) {
            console.error(`Error: ${err}`);
            Sentry.captureException(err);
            return [null, err as Error];
        }
    }
}

import { useEffect, useState, useCallback, useRef } from "react";
import { useNavigate, useSearchParams } from "react-router";
import { loadStripe } from "@stripe/stripe-js";
import {
    EmbeddedCheckoutProvider,
    EmbeddedCheckout,
} from "@stripe/react-stripe-js";
import { H1 } from "@/components/ui/h1";
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton";
import { Card } from "@/components/ui/card";
import { useApp } from "@/app/providers/app-provider";
import type { PLAN_IDS } from "@/lib/application/PaymentManager";
import { trackGoogleAnalyticsEvent } from "@/lib/analytics/google-analytics";

// Make sure to call `loadStripe` outside of a component’s render to avoid
// recreating the `Stripe` object on every render.
// This is your test secret API key.
const stripePromise = loadStripe(import.meta.env.VITE_STRIPE_PUBLIC_KEY);

const CheckoutForm = ({ clientSecret }: { clientSecret: string }) => (
    <EmbeddedCheckoutProvider stripe={stripePromise} options={{ clientSecret }}>
        <EmbeddedCheckout />
    </EmbeddedCheckoutProvider>
);

const CheckoutSkeleton = () => <Skeleton className="h-48" />;

const Checkout = () => {
    const [clientSecret, setClientSecret] = useState<string | null>(null);
    const [error, setError] = useState<string>("");
    const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
    // A ref rather than state so the slot is claimed in the same tick. State
    // updates land after the await below, which would let a re-render start a
    // second checkout session and report a second begin_checkout.
    const hasCreatedSession = useRef(false);

    const { appStore, paymentManager } = useApp();
    const { session } = appStore;
    const [searchParams] = useSearchParams();
    const navigate = useNavigate();

    const planId = searchParams.get("planId") as keyof typeof PLAN_IDS;

    // Memoize the checkout session creation function
    const createCheckoutSession = useCallback(async () => {
        if (hasCreatedSession.current || !session?.access_token || !planId) {
            return;
        }

        hasCreatedSession.current = true;
        setIsLoading(true);
        setError("");

        try {
            const [data, error] = await paymentManager.createCheckoutSession(planId);

            if (error) {
                // Releasing the slot lets a later render retry a transient failure.
                hasCreatedSession.current = false;
                setError(error.message || "Failed to create checkout session");
                return;
            }

            if (data?.clientSecret) {
                setClientSecret(data.clientSecret);
                trackGoogleAnalyticsEvent("begin_checkout", { plan_id: planId });
            } else {
                setError("Invalid response from payment service");
            }
        } catch (err) {
            hasCreatedSession.current = false;
            setError(
                err instanceof Error ? err.message : "An unexpected error occurred",
            );
        } finally {
            setIsLoading(false);
        }
    }, [session?.access_token, planId, paymentManager]);

    useEffect(() => {
        // Early validation and redirects
        if (!session?.access_token) {
            navigate("/home");
            return;
        }

        if (!planId) {
            navigate("/pricing");
            return;
        }

        createCheckoutSession();
    }, [session?.access_token, planId, navigate, createCheckoutSession]);

    // Render content based on current state
    let content: React.ReactNode;
    if (isLoading || (!clientSecret && !error)) {
        content = <CheckoutSkeleton />;
    } else if (error) {
        content = (
            <Card className="border-destructive text-destructive p-4 w-full text-balance">
                {error}
            </Card>
        );
    } else if (clientSecret) {
        content = <CheckoutForm clientSecret={clientSecret} />;
    }

    return (
        <div>
            <section className="flex flex-col gap-4 lg:max-w-3xl mb-6">
                <H1>Checkout</H1>
            </section>
            <div>{content}</div>
        </div>
    );
};

export default Checkout;

                                <Label
                                    htmlFor="no-trial"
                                    className="cursor-pointer leading-relaxed"
                                >

                                    }
                                    className="mt-1"

                                <Label
                                    htmlFor="no-refunds"
                                    className="cursor-pointer leading-relaxed"
                                >

                                    <strong className="text-destructive">

                                    </strong>{" "}

                            <div className="flex items-start gap-3">

                </Card>

        </div>

import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare";
import type { Bindings } from "../../bindings";
import { getEmailService } from "../lib/email-service";
import { reportError } from "../utils/reportError";

export interface UserMetaData {
    id: string;
    email: string;
    subscription: {
        id: string;
        status: string;
        end_date: string;
        interval: string;
        planTier: string;
        start_date: string;
    };
}

export function computeRenewalWindow(now: Date): {
    windowStart: Date;
    windowEnd: Date;
} {
    const windowStart = new Date(now.getTime() + 29 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    windowStart.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    const windowEnd = new Date(now.getTime() + 31 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    windowEnd.setUTCHours(23, 59, 59, 999);
    return { windowStart, windowEnd };
}

export function filterEligibleUsers(
    users: UserMetaData[],
    windowStart: Date,
    windowEnd: Date,
): UserMetaData[] {
    return users.filter((user) => {
        const endDate = new Date(user.subscription.end_date);

        return endDate >= windowStart && endDate <= windowEnd;
    });
}

export async function handleScheduledRenewalReminders(
    env: Bindings,
): Promise<void> {
    try {
        console.log("env cache", env.MAIN_CACHE);
        const emailService = getEmailService(env);
        const supabase = createClient(
            env.SUPABASE_URL,
            env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY,
        );

        const now = new Date();
        const { windowStart, windowEnd } = computeRenewalWindow(now);

        // Query for active yearly subscribers
        const { data, error } = await supabase
            .from("user_meta_data")
            .select("id, email, subscription")
            .not("subscription", "is", null)
            .filter("subscription->>status", "eq", "active")
            .filter("subscription->>interval", "eq", "YEAR");

        if (error) {
            console.error("Failed to query user_meta_data:", error);
            reportError(error);
            return;
        }

        if (!data || data.length === 0) {
            console.log("Renewal reminder: no active yearly subscribers found.");
            return;
        }

        // Filter for end_date within the target window (in JS to avoid PostgREST date edge cases)
        const eligibleUsers = filterEligibleUsers(
            data as UserMetaData[],
            windowStart,
            windowEnd,
        );

        console.log(
            `Renewal reminder: ${eligibleUsers.length} eligible out of ${data.length} active yearly subscribers.`,
        );

        let sent = 0;
        let skipped = 0;
        let errors = 0;

        for (const user of eligibleUsers) {
            console.log(
                `Processing user ${user.id} with subscription end date ${user.subscription.end_date}`,
            );

            const endDateStr = user.subscription.end_date.split("T")[0];
            const kvKey = `renewal-reminder:${user.id}:${endDateStr}`;

            try {
                // Idempotency check
                const existing = await env.MAIN_CACHE.get(kvKey);
                if (existing) {
                    skipped++;
                    continue;
                }

                await emailService.sendSubscriptionRenewalEmail({
                    emailAddress: user.email,
                    endDate: user.subscription.end_date,
                    planTier: user.subscription.planTier ?? "PREMIUM",
                });

                // Record send in KV with 45-day TTL
                await env.MAIN_CACHE.put(kvKey, new Date().toISOString(), {
                    expirationTtl: 45 * 24 * 60 * 60,
                });

                sent++;
            } catch (err) {
                errors++;
                console.error(`Renewal reminder: failed for user ${user.id}:`, err);
                reportError(err);
            }
        }

        console.log(
            `Renewal reminder complete: ${sent} sent, ${skipped} skipped, ${errors} errors.`,
        );
    } catch (err) {
        console.error("Renewal reminder: top-level error:", err);
        reportError(err);
    } finally {
        await Sentry.flush();
    }
}

import { type Context, type ExecutionContext, Hono } from "hono";
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare";
import { applyMiddleware } from "./middlewares";
import attributionRouter from "./routes/attribution-router";
import authRouter from "./routes/auth";
import userRouter from "./routes/user";
import paymentRouter from "./routes/payment";
import contactRouter from "./routes/contact";
import type { Bindings } from "../bindings";
import audioRouter from "./routes/audio-router";
import favoriteTracksRouter from "./routes/favorite-tracks-router";
import listeningRouter from "./routes/listening-router";
import rewardsRouter from "./routes/rewards-router";
import { handleScheduledRenewalReminders } from "./scheduled/renewalReminder";

// initialize the app
const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Bindings }>();

// add sensible security and app defaults
applyMiddleware(app);

// Health check route
app.get("/", async (c: Context) => c.json({ message: "Working." }));

// Routes alphabetically
app.route("/attribution", attributionRouter);
app.route("/audio", audioRouter);
app.route("/auth", authRouter);
app.route("/contact", contactRouter);
app.route("/user/favorite-tracks", favoriteTracksRouter);
app.route("/listening", listeningRouter);
app.route("/payment", paymentRouter);
app.route("/rewards", rewardsRouter);
app.route("/user", userRouter);

// Full ExportedHandler with fetch (Hono) and scheduled (cron) support
const handler = {
    fetch: app.fetch,
    scheduled: async (
        _controller: ScheduledController,
        env: Bindings,
        ctx: ExecutionContext,
    ) => {
        ctx.waitUntil(handleScheduledRenewalReminders(env));
    },
};

// wrap sentry around the handler for error monitoring
export default Sentry.withSentry((env: Bindings) => {
    if (!env.SENTRY_DSN || !env.ENVIRONMENT) {
        throw new Error("SENTRY_DSN and ENVIRONMENT are required.");
    }

    return {
        dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN,
        // Set tracesSampleRate to 1.0 to capture 100% of spans for tracing.
        tracesSampleRate: env.ENVIRONMENT === "production" ? 1.0 : 0,
        environment: env.ENVIRONMENT,
    };
}, handler);
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare";

export function reportError(error: unknown): void {
    try {
        Sentry.captureException(error);
    } catch (reportingError) {
        console.error("Error reporting route error:", reportingError);
    }
}
import type { CloudflareOptions } from "@sentry/cloudflare";
import {
    sanitizeProviderMessage,
    type EmailFailureReporterEnv,
} from "./email-failure-reporter";

export const createEmailSentryOptions = (
    env: EmailFailureReporterEnv,
): CloudflareOptions => ({
    dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN,
    enabled: Boolean(env.SENTRY_DSN),
    environment: env.ENVIRONMENT,
    sendDefaultPii: false,
    tracesSampleRate: 1,
    enableLogs: true,
    beforeSend(event) {
        if (event.tags?.email_failure_source !== "provider_send") {
            return null;
        }
        const providerMessage = event.extra?.provider_message;

        return {
            ...(event.event_id ? { event_id: event.event_id } : {}),
            ...(event.timestamp ? { timestamp: event.timestamp } : {}),
            ...(event.platform ? { platform: event.platform } : {}),
            ...(event.level ? { level: event.level } : {}),
            ...(event.exception ? { exception: event.exception } : {}),
            ...(event.tags ? { tags: event.tags } : {}),
            ...(event.environment ? { environment: event.environment } : {}),
            ...(typeof providerMessage === "string" && providerMessage
                ? {
                        extra: {
                            provider_message: sanitizeProviderMessage(providerMessage),
                        },
                    }
                : {}),
        } as typeof event;
    },
});
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare";

type ErrorContext = {
    source: string;
    payload: unknown;
    messageId?: string;
};

/**
 * Provider-agnostic error reporting wrapper for queue and DLQ failures.
 * The current implementation uses Sentry under the hood.
 */
export const reportError = (
    env: Env,
    ctx: ExecutionContext,
    handler: "webhooks-consumer" | "webhooks-dlq",
    error: unknown,
    context: ErrorContext,
): void => {
    if (!env.SENTRY_DSN) return;

    const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));

    try {
        Sentry.withScope((scope) => {
            scope.setTag("handler", handler);
            scope.setTag("source", context.source);
            if (context.messageId) {
                scope.setTag("message_id", context.messageId);
            }

            scope.setContext("webhook", {
                handler,
                source: context.source,
                messageId: context.messageId,
                environment: env.ENVIRONMENT,
            });
            scope.setExtra("payload", context.payload);

            Sentry.captureException(err);
        });

        ctx.waitUntil(Sentry.flush(2000));
    } catch (reportingError) {
        console.error("Error reporting worker error:", reportingError);
    }
};
import type { MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";

const DEFAULT_REDACTED_HEADERS = new Set([
    "authorization",
    "cookie",
    "set-cookie",
    "x-api-key",
]);

const humanize = (times: string[]) => {
    const [delimiter, separator] = [",", "."];
    const orderedTimes = times.map((value) =>
        value.replace(/(\d)(?=(\d\d\d)+(?!\d))/g, `$1${delimiter}`),
    );
    return orderedTimes.join(separator);
};

const formatDuration = (start: number) => {
    const delta = Date.now() - start;
    return humanize([delta < 1e3 ? `${delta}ms` : `${Math.round(delta / 1e3)}s`]);
};

const formatStatus = (status: number) => `${status}`;

const captureHeaders = (
    headers: Headers,
    redacted: Set<string>,
): Record<string, string> => {
    const result: Record<string, string> = {};
    headers.forEach((value, key) => {
        result[key] = redacted.has(key.toLowerCase()) ? "[redacted]" : value;
    });
    return result;
};

const buildPath = (url: string) => {
    const parsedUrl = new URL(url);
    return `${parsedUrl.pathname}${parsedUrl.search}`;
};

const escapeRegex = (value: string) =>
    value.replace(/[|\\{}()[\]^$+?.]/g, "\\$&");

const compilePathPattern = (pattern: string) => {
    const regexSource = escapeRegex(pattern)
        .replace(/\*\*/g, ".*")
        .replace(/\*/g, "[^?]*");

    return new RegExp(`^${regexSource}$`);
};

const tryParseJsonBody = async (bodyCarrier: Request | Response) => {
    try {
        return await bodyCarrier.clone().json();
    } catch {
        return "[unreadable]";
    }
};

const logIncoming = async (
    fn: (msg: string) => void,
    method: string,
    path: string,
    headers: Record<string, string>,
    body: unknown,
) => {
    const parts = [`[REQUEST] ${method} ${path}`];
    if (Object.keys(headers).length > 0) {
        parts.push(JSON.stringify(headers));
    }
    if (body !== undefined) {
        parts.push(JSON.stringify(body));
    }
    fn(parts.join(" "));
};

const logOutgoing = async (
    fn: (msg: string) => void,
    method: string,
    path: string,
    status: number,
    elapsed: string,
) => {
    fn(`[RESPONSE] ${method} ${path} ${formatStatus(status)} ${elapsed}`);
};

export type RequestLoggerOptions = {
    fn?: (msg: string) => void;
    ignoredPaths?: string[];
    redactedHeaders?: string[];
    logRequestBody?: boolean;
    logResponseBody?: boolean;
};

export const createRequestLogger = ({
    fn = console.log,
    ignoredPaths = [],
    redactedHeaders = [],
    logRequestBody = true,
    logResponseBody = true,
}: RequestLoggerOptions = {}): MiddlewareHandler => {
    const matchers = ignoredPaths.map((pattern) => compilePathPattern(pattern));
    const isIgnored = (path: string) =>
        matchers.some((match) => match.test(path));
    const redacted = new Set([
        ...DEFAULT_REDACTED_HEADERS,
        ...redactedHeaders.map((header) => header.toLowerCase()),
    ]);

    const requestLogger: MiddlewareHandler = async (c, next) => {
        const { method, raw } = c.req;
        const path = buildPath(raw.url);
        const ignored = isIgnored(path);
        const reqHeaders = ignored ? {} : captureHeaders(raw.headers, redacted);

        let reqBody: unknown;
        const reqContentType = c.req.header("content-type") ?? "";
        if (
            logRequestBody &&
            ["POST", "PUT", "PATCH"].includes(method) &&
            reqContentType.includes("application/json")
        ) {
            reqBody = ignored ? "[redacted]" : await tryParseJsonBody(raw);
        }

        await logIncoming(fn, method, path, reqHeaders, reqBody);

        const start = Date.now();
        await next();
        const elapsed = formatDuration(start);
        const durationMs = Date.now() - start;

        await logOutgoing(fn, method, path, c.res.status, elapsed);

        let resBody: unknown;
        const resContentType = c.res.headers.get("content-type") ?? "";
        if (logResponseBody && resContentType.includes("application/json")) {
            resBody = ignored ? "[redacted]" : await tryParseJsonBody(c.res);
        }

        fn(
            `[FULL LOG] ${JSON.stringify({
                ts: new Date().toISOString(),
                method,
                path,
                status: c.res.status,
                durationMs,
                req: {
                    headers: reqHeaders,
                    body: reqBody,
                },
                res: {
                    body: resBody,
                },
            })}
        `,
        );
    };

    return requestLogger;
};

import Stripe from "stripe";
import type { Hono } from "hono";
import { createRequestLogger } from "@coffitivity/hono-request-logger";
import { cors } from "hono/cors";
import { secureHeaders } from "hono/secure-headers";
import { AttributionRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/attribution/AttributionRepository";
import { UserRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/users/UserRepository";
import { UserD1Database } from "./repositories/adapters/users/UserDatabase";
import { UserKvCache } from "./repositories/adapters/users/UserCache";
import { AudioRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/audios/AudioRepository";
import { AudioD1Database } from "./repositories/adapters/audios/AudioDatabase";
import { FavoriteTrackRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/favoriteTracks/FavoriteTrackRepository";
import { ListeningSessionRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/listening/ListeningSessionRepository";
import { PlanRecordRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/plans/PlanRecordRepository";
import { RewardsRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/rewards/RewardsRepository";
import { ReferralRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/rewards/ReferralRepository";
import { RewardNotificationRepository } from "./repositories/adapters/rewards/RewardNotificationRepository";
import { HTTPException } from "hono/http-exception";
import type { ContentfulStatusCode } from "hono/utils/http-status";
import { userDb, appDataDb } from "./repositories/d1";
import type { Bindings } from "../bindings";
import { supabaseClient } from "./repositories/supabase";
import { reportError } from "./utils/reportError";

export const applyMiddleware = (
    app: Hono<{ Bindings: Bindings }>,
): Hono<{ Bindings: Bindings }> => {
    app.use(
        createRequestLogger({
            ignoredPaths: ["/ping"],
        }),
    );

    // CORS middleware
    app.use(
        "*",
        cors({
            origin: [
                "https://coffitivity.com",
                "https://staging.coffitivity.com",
                "https://the-buzz.coffitivity.com",
                "https://www.coffitivity.com",
                "http://localhost:4321",
                "http://localhost:5173",
            ],
            credentials: true,
            allowMethods: ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"],
        }),
    );

    // Secure headers middleware
    app.use(secureHeaders());

    // Attach access to the users repository to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        const userDatabase = new UserD1Database(userDb);
        const userCache = new UserKvCache(c.env.MAIN_CACHE);
        const repo = new UserRepository(userDatabase, userCache);

        c.set("userRepo", repo);

        await next();
    });

    // Attach access to the audio repository to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        const audioDatabase = new AudioD1Database(appDataDb);
        const repo = new AudioRepository(audioDatabase);

        c.set("audioRepo", repo);

        await next();
    });

    // Attach access to the listening session repository to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        const repo = new ListeningSessionRepository(appDataDb);

        c.set("listeningRepo", repo);

        await next();
    });

    // Attach access to the Plan Record repository to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        c.set("planRecordRepo", new PlanRecordRepository(appDataDb));

        await next();
    });

    // Attach access to the Favorite Track repository to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        c.set("favoriteTrackRepo", new FavoriteTrackRepository(appDataDb));

        await next();
    });

    // Attach access to the rewards repositories to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        c.set("rewardsRepo", new RewardsRepository(appDataDb));
        c.set("referralRepo", new ReferralRepository(appDataDb));
        c.set(
            "rewardNotificationRepo",
            new RewardNotificationRepository(appDataDb),
        );

        await next();
    });

    // Attach access to the attribution ledger to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        c.set("attributionRepo", new AttributionRepository(appDataDb));

        await next();
    });

    // attach stripe to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        const stripe = new Stripe(c.env.STRIPE_KEY, {
            apiVersion: "2025-02-24.acacia",
        });
        c.set("stripe", stripe);

        await next();
    });

    // attach Supabase client to the context
    app.use(async (c, next) => {
        c.set("supabase", supabaseClient);
        await next();
    });

    // Debugger
    // app.use(async (c, next) => {
    //     console.log('Request:', c.req);

    //     await next();
    // });

    // Rate limiter middleware
    // app.use(async (c, next) => {
    //     const { success } = await c.env.FLAT_RATE_LIMITER.limit({ key: "*" }); // limit all requests
    //     if (!success) {
    //         reportError(new Error("Exceeded Rate limiting"));

    //         return c.json({ message: "Rate limit exceeded." }, 429);
    //     }

    //     await next();
    // });

    // Not found middleware
    app.notFound((c) => c.json({ message: "Not Found." }, 404));

    // Error handling middleware
    app.onError((err, c) => {
        console.error(err);
        // If the error is an HTTPException, return the response from the error - mostly for JWT auth validation
        if (err instanceof HTTPException) {
            const res = err.getResponse();
            const cause = err.cause;

            console.log("Error cause:", cause);

            return c.json(
                { message: res.statusText },
                res.status as ContentfulStatusCode,
            );
        }

        reportError(err);
        return c.json({ message: "Internal Server Error." }, 500);
    });

    return app;
};

import { index, int, sqliteTable, text } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";

/**
 * Referral visits table — records each visit from an affiliate link.
 *
 * Used for auditing, deduplication, and referral count queries.
 * Deduplication is based on (referrerUserId, visitorFingerprint) —
 * same visitor clicking the same referrer's link multiple times = 1 credit.
 *
 * referrerUserId stores Supabase auth UIDs (plain text, no FK).
 */
export const referralVisits = sqliteTable(
    "referral_visits_table",
    {
        // Primary key - ULID
        id: text().primaryKey().notNull(),

        // Supabase auth UID of the user who shared the link
        referrerUserId: text().notNull(),

        // Cookie-based fingerprint for deduplication
        visitorFingerprint: text().notNull(),

        // Visitor IP address (for analytics, not dedup)
        ipAddress: text(),

        // Visitor user agent (for analytics)
        userAgent: text(),

        // The URL the visitor landed on
        landingPage: text(),

        // Whether this visit was credited (false if duplicate or cap reached)
        credited: int({ mode: "boolean" }).notNull().default(false),

        // Visit timestamp (ISO 8601)
        createdAt: text().notNull(),
    },
    (table) => [
        index("rv_referrer_idx").on(table.referrerUserId),
        index("rv_dedup_idx").on(table.referrerUserId, table.visitorFingerprint),
    ],
);
import { index, int, sqliteTable, text } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";

/**
 * Attribution events table — the immutable acquisition-measurement ledger.
 *
 * One row per Attribution Event. Both Attribution Touches (arrivals carrying
 * campaign parameters) and the funnel steps that follow them live here, so a
 * Coffitivity User's history reads as a single ordered sequence:
 *
 *   touch -> signup -> trial_started -> payment -> subscription_ended -> touch
 *
 * Measurement fields are append-only. Account deletion anonymizes its rows by
 * clearing the user, visitor, and Stripe links while retaining aggregate facts.
 *
 * Deliberately has no unique constraints. "First payment" is the earliest
 * `payment` row at read time, not a schema rule — that keeps first-touch vs
 * last-touch, and acquisition vs renewal, as questions the reader answers
 * rather than decisions baked into writes.
 *
 * Deliberately stores no IP address and no raw user agent. The user agent is
 * reduced to `deviceType` when the row is written and the string discarded.
 */
export const attributionEvents = sqliteTable(
    "attribution_events_table",
    {
        id: text().primaryKey().notNull(),

        // Browser-held identifier from the coff_vid cookie.

/**
 * Listening sessions table tracks per-track, per-user playback sessions.
 *
 * Each row represents a single play→pause (or play→unload) event.
 * - `endedAt` is NULL while a session is in progress.
 * - `durationSeconds` is computed when the session ends.
 * - Orphaned sessions (null endedAt) are auto-closed on the next `POST /listening/start`.
 * - Session IDs are client-generated ULIDs sent in the start request.
 */
export const listeningSessions = sqliteTable(
    "listening_sessions_table",
    {
        // Primary key - client-generated ULID
        id: text().primaryKey().unique().notNull(),

        // Owner user ID (indexed for daily usage queries)
        userId: text().notNull(),

        // Track/soundscape identifier
        trackId: text().notNull(),

        // When playback started (ISO 8601)
        startedAt: text().notNull(),

        // When playback stopped (ISO 8601) - NULL means in-progress
        endedAt: text(),

        // Computed on session close: endedAt - startedAt in seconds
        durationSeconds: int(),

        // Row creation timestamp (ISO 8601)
        createdAt: text().notNull(),
    },
    (table) => [
        index("ls_user_date_idx").on(table.userId, table.startedAt),
        index("ls_user_track_idx").on(table.userId, table.trackId),
    ],
);

 *
 * Schema design:
 * - Queryable columns: id, slug, userId, releaseDate, createdAt, updatedAt

    "custom_blends_table",

        userId: text(),

        // Release date for sorting (ISO datetime string)

        // Timestamps

        updatedAt: text().notNull(),

        // - isLooping: boolean
        // - location: { ... } | null
        // - albumId: string
        // - imageUrlStub: string
        // - collectionId: string
        data: text().notNull(),
    },
    (table) => [
        index("slug_idx").on(table.slug),
        index("user_id_idx").on(table.userId),
        index("release_date_idx").on(table.releaseDate),

/**
 * POST /rewards/referral — Records a referral visit. Unauthenticated endpoint.
 */
rewardsRouter.post(
    "/referral",
    validator("json", (value, c) => {
        const parsed = referralSchema.safeParse(value);
        if (!parsed.success) {
            return c.json(
                {
                    success: false,
                    code: API_ERROR_NAMES.BAD_REQUEST,
                    message: "Invalid payload.",
                } as ApiError,
                400,
            );
        }
        return parsed.data;
    }),
    async (c): Promise<TypedResponse<ApiResponse<ReferralResponse>>> => {
        try {
            const { referralCode, fingerprint, landingPage, userAgent } =
                c.req.valid("json");

            const rewardsRepo = c.get("rewardsRepo");
            const referralRepo = c.get("referralRepo");

            // Resolve referral code to user ID
            const referrerUserId =
                await rewardsRepo.getUserByReferralCode(referralCode);

            if (!referrerUserId) {
                return c.json(
                    {
                        success: false,
                        code: API_ERROR_NAMES.NOT_FOUND,
                        message: "Invalid referral code.",
                    },
                    404,
                );
            }

            // Prevent self-referrals: if the visitor is logged in and is the referrer, reject
            const accessToken = c.req.header("Authorization")?.split(" ")[1];
            if (accessToken) {
                const { data: authData } = await c
                    .get("supabase")
                    .auth.getUser(accessToken);
                if (authData?.user?.id === referrerUserId) {
                    return c.json(
                        {
                            success: true,
                            data: { isCredited: false, reason: "self_referral" },
                        },
                        200,
                    );
                }
            }

            // Check deduplication
            const isDuplicate = await referralRepo.isDuplicate(
                referrerUserId,
                fingerprint,
            );

            if (isDuplicate) {
                return c.json(
                    {
                        success: true,
                        data: { isCredited: false, reason: "duplicate" },
                    },
                    200,
                );
            }

            // Check lifetime cap
            const userReward = await rewardsRepo.getOrCreateUserReward(
                referrerUserId,
                "affiliate-referral",
            );

            const reward = (await rewardsRepo.getActiveRewards()).find(
                (r) => r.id === "affiliate-referral",
            );

            if (reward && userReward.totalSecondsEarned >= reward.maxSeconds) {
                // Still record the visit but don't credit
                await referralRepo.recordVisit({
                    referrerUserId,
                    visitorFingerprint: fingerprint,
                    ipAddress: c.req.header("CF-Connecting-IP") ?? null,
                    userAgent: userAgent ?? null,
                    landingPage: landingPage ?? null,
                });

                return c.json(
                    {
                        success: true,
                        data: { isCredited: false, reason: "cap_reached" },
                    },
                    200,
                );
            }

            // Record the visit
            await referralRepo.recordVisit({
                referrerUserId,
                visitorFingerprint: fingerprint,
                ipAddress: c.req.header("CF-Connecting-IP") ?? null,
                userAgent: userAgent ?? null,
                landingPage: landingPage ?? null,
            });

            // Increment reward
            const rewardSeconds = reward?.rewardSeconds ?? 900;
            await rewardsRepo.incrementRewardEarned(
                referrerUserId,
                "affiliate-referral",
                rewardSeconds,
            );

            return c.json(
                {
                    success: true,
                    data: { isCredited: true, secondsEarned: rewardSeconds },
                },
                200,
            );
        } catch (error) {
            console.error("Error recording referral:", error);
            reportError(error);
            return c.json(
                {
                    success: false,
                    code: API_ERROR_NAMES.SERVER_ERROR,
                    message: "Error recording referral.",
                },
                500,
            );
        }
    },
);

import { useEffect } from "react";
import Cookies from "universal-cookie";
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react";
import { useApp } from "./app-provider";

export const FINGERPRINT_COOKIE_NAME = "coff_fp";
export const FINGERPRINT_MAX_AGE = 60 * 60 * 24 * 365; // 1 year in seconds

export function getOrCreateFingerprint(
    cookieJar: Cookies = new Cookies(),
): string {
    const existing = cookieJar.get(FINGERPRINT_COOKIE_NAME);
    if (existing) return existing;

    const fingerprint = crypto.randomUUID();
    cookieJar.set(FINGERPRINT_COOKIE_NAME, fingerprint, {
        maxAge: FINGERPRINT_MAX_AGE,
        path: "/",
        sameSite: "lax",
    });
    return fingerprint;
}

/**
 * Checks the current URL for a `ref` query param and, if present,
 * records the referral visit via the provided callback, then cleans the URL.
 *
 * Returns true if a referral was detected, false otherwise.
 */
export function processReferral(
    location: { search: string; pathname: string; hash: string },
    userAgent: string,
    recordFn: (
        code: string,
        fingerprint: string,
        landingPage: string,
        userAgent: string,
    ) => Promise<unknown>,
    cookieJar?: Cookies,
): boolean {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
    const referralCode = params.get("ref");

    if (!referralCode) return false;

    const fingerprint = getOrCreateFingerprint(cookieJar);

    recordFn(referralCode, fingerprint, location.pathname, userAgent).catch(
        (error) => {
            Sentry.captureException(error);
        },
    );

    // Remove ref param from URL to keep it clean
    params.delete("ref");
    const newSearch = params.toString();
    const newUrl = `${location.pathname}${newSearch ? `?${newSearch}` : ""}${location.hash}`;
    window.history.replaceState({}, "", newUrl);

    return true;
}

export default function ReferralProvider({
    children,
}: {
    children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
    const { appManager } = useApp();

    useEffect(() => {
        processReferral(
            window.location,
            navigator.userAgent,
            appManager.recordReferral,
        );
    }, [appManager.recordReferral]);

    return <>{children}</>;
}
import { useEffect } from "react";
import type Cookies from "universal-cookie";
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react";
import { getOrCreateVisitorId } from "@/app/attribution/visitor-id";
import type { AttributionTouch } from "@coffitivity/shared";
import { useApp } from "./app-provider";

/** Query parameters that mark an arrival as campaign-driven. */
const CAMPAIGN_PARAMS = {
    utm_source: "source",
    utm_medium: "medium",
    utm_campaign: "campaign",
    utm_content: "content",
    utm_term: "term",
    gclid: "gclid",
} as const;

/**
 * `gclid` is read but deliberately left in the address bar.
 *
 * Google's tag loads async, so its inline `config` call only queues work — the
 * click id is not read off the URL, and `_gcl_aw` is not set, until
 * googletagmanager.com has downloaded and run. Our bundle is local and may be
 * cached, so stripping the click id here can beat Google's tag to it and
 * silently break the conversion import that a later build depends on.
 *
 * The reasons for stripping barely apply to it anyway: a click id is unique per
 * click, so a shared URL carrying one cannot mint an entire fake campaign the
 * way a shared `utm_campaign` can.
 */
const PARAMS_TO_STRIP = Object.keys(CAMPAIGN_PARAMS).filter(
    (param) => param !== "gclid",
);

/**
 * Records an Attribution Touch when the current URL carries campaign
 * parameters, then removes the utm parameters from the address bar.
 *
 * Nothing happens — and no identifier is stored — for an ordinary visit, so
 * routine browsing leaves nothing behind.
 *
 * Stripping matters for two reasons: a hard refresh is a fresh mount that would
 * otherwise re-read the same parameters and record the arrival twice, and a URL
 * copied out of the address bar into a chat or a bookmark would keep minting
 * paid-campaign touches for people who never saw the ad. `gclid` is the
 * exception and stays — see PARAMS_TO_STRIP.
 *
 * Returns true if a touch was recorded.
 */
export function processAttribution(
    location: { search: string; pathname: string; hash: string },
    referrer: string,
    recordFn: (_touch: AttributionTouch) => Promise<unknown>,
    cookieJar?: Cookies,
): boolean {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);

    const campaign: Partial<AttributionTouch> = {};
    let hasCampaignParam = false;

    for (const [param, field] of Object.entries(CAMPAIGN_PARAMS)) {
        const value = params.get(param);
        if (value) {
            campaign[field] = value;
            hasCampaignParam = true;
        }
    }

    if (!hasCampaignParam) return false;

    const visitorId = getOrCreateVisitorId(cookieJar);

    recordFn({
        visitorId,
        ...campaign,
        landingPage: location.pathname,
        referrer,
    }).catch((error) => {
        Sentry.captureException(error);
    });

    // Only our own parameters are removed — anything else the URL carried, the
    // referral code and Google's click id included, is left for its owner.
    for (const param of PARAMS_TO_STRIP) {
        params.delete(param);
    }

    const newSearch = params.toString();
    const newUrl = `${location.pathname}${newSearch ? `?${newSearch}` : ""}${location.hash}`;
    window.history.replaceState({}, "", newUrl);

    return true;
}

export default function AttributionProvider({
    children,
}: {
    children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
    const { appManager } = useApp();

    useEffect(() => {
        processAttribution(
            window.location,
            document.referrer,
            appManager.recordAttributionTouch,
        );
    }, [appManager.recordAttributionTouch]);

    return <>{children}</>;
}

Two direct contradictions have surfaced: referral/attribution code uses location data for analytics even though the Privacy Policy says location/IP are used only for security and infrastructure, and the OTP “sign-in” flow can create new accounts without showing or recording Terms/age acceptance. I’m checking the linked security commitments and the rest of the deletion/retention path before ranking the findings.

FILE=Security Incident Response.pdf PAGES=4

=== PAGE 1 ===

Security Incident Response
As of August 20, 2026
This document describes how Coffitivity identifies, responds to, and communicates about
security incidents affecting personal information. It reflects our practices as of the version date
and may change as our Services and infrastructure evolve. It is a description of practice and is
not a contractual commitment; where a written agreement between Coffitivity and a customer
sets specific incident obligations, that agreement governs.
1. What we treat as a security incident
A security incident is an event that leads to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, or unauthorized disclosure of or access to personal information held by Coffitivity or
by a service provider acting on our behalf.
The following are not security incidents, and do not trigger this process:
●
●
●
●
Unsuccessful login attempts, credential-stuffing attempts, and other blocked
authentication activity
Port scans, pings, denial-of-service attempts, and comparable network activity that our
infrastructure absorbs or blocks
Vulnerability reports where there is no evidence that personal information was accessed
Service outages or degradation that do not involve personal information
2. What is at risk
Our exposure in an incident is bounded by how little we hold. For individual accounts, this is an
email address, a password hash, a payment-processor customer identifier and related
transaction metadata, and usage data. Full payment card details are handled by our payment
processor and are never received or stored by Coffitivity. IP addresses and browser user agents
are processed at the network edge for delivery and abuse prevention.
Where the Services are provided through a school, school board, employer, or similar
organization, access is delivered through single sign-on or through session credentials issued
and controlled by that organization. In that model Coffitivity does not receive or store names,
email addresses, dates of birth, student or employee identifiers, academic records, or any
comparable personal information about the organization's users, and no individual account is
created.
3. How we detect incidents

=== PAGE 2 ===

●
●
●
●
●
Application error and exception monitoring (Sentry)
Network, edge, and access monitoring provided by our hosting and security provider
(Cloudflare)
Notifications from our service providers regarding incidents affecting their systems
Reports from users, customers, and security researchers sent to legal@coffitivity.com
Internal review during routine operations and deployment
4. Severity
Level Definition
High Confirmed unauthorized access to, disclosure of, or loss of personal information;
or any incident involving information associated with an organizational account or
with users who are minors
Medium Credible indication of exposure that investigation has not yet confirmed or ruled
out
Low Incident with no involvement of personal information, or exposure fully contained
before any access occurred
Severity is assessed on first review and reassessed as facts develop.
5. Response
6. Contain. Take immediate steps to stop ongoing exposure — revoking credentials or
tokens, disabling affected functionality, or blocking traffic.
7. Assess. Establish what happened, what information was involved, whose information it
was, over what period, and whether exposure is ongoing.
8. Remediate. Fix the underlying cause and restore affected systems and data.
9. Communicate. Determine who must be informed and provide notice as described in
Section 6.
10. Close. Confirm remediation, complete the incident record, and conduct the review
described in Section 7.
Coffitivity is a small company. The founder is the accountable owner of every incident and
directs the response. Depending on the incident, we escalate to outside legal counsel and to the
support and security teams of the affected service provider, and we engage external technical
assistance where the incident exceeds our internal capacity.
11. Notification

=== PAGE 3 ===

Individuals. Where an incident is likely to create a meaningful risk to an individual, we notify
that person without undue delay after confirming the incident and establishing its scope, by
email to the address associated with their account and, where appropriate, by notice within the
Services.
Organizations. Where an organization provides access to the Services for its users, we notify
that organization's designated contact of any incident affecting information associated with its
account, and we provide enough detail for the organization to assess the incident and meet its
own obligations. Where the organization's users include minors, we notify the organization and
do not contact students or their families directly, so that the organization retains control of
communication with the individuals in its care. Where an agreement with an organization
specifies a notification timeframe, that timeframe governs.
Regulators. We report an incident to a supervisory or regulatory authority where we are legally
required to do so. Where an organization provides access to the Services, that organization is
normally the party holding the reporting relationship with its own regulator, and our role is to
support that organization with the information it needs rather than to report independently.
Content of a notice. To the extent known at the time, a notice states what happened and when,
what categories of information were involved, how many individuals or records were affected,
what we have done to contain and remediate the incident, what we recommend recipients do,
and a contact point for questions. We provide updates as the investigation develops.
7. Records and review
We maintain a record of security incidents, including those that do not require notification,
covering what occurred, how it was assessed, what was done, and what was communicated.
Following a High or Medium severity incident we conduct a review to identify the root cause and
the changes needed to prevent recurrence, and we track those changes to completion.
8. Supporting security controls
●
●
●
●
●
●
Encryption in transit. All communication with the Services uses TLS.
Encryption at rest. Personal information stored with our infrastructure providers is
encrypted at rest.
Credentials. Passwords are stored only as cryptographic hashes and are never stored
or accessible in readable form.
Payments. Card data is handled entirely by a PCI-DSS Level 1 certified payment
processor.
Access control. Access to production systems and personal information is limited to
authorized personnel with a need to know.
Provider diligence. We assess the security posture of our service providers and require
appropriate contractual security commitments.

=== PAGE 4 ===

9. Questions
Questions about this document, or reports of a suspected security issue, should be sent to
legal@coffitivity.com.
Revision history: Version 1.0 — 08/20/26 — initial publication.

=== PAGE 1 ===

CUSTOMER ASSURANCE STATEMENT
Security & Privacy Overview
A plain-language description of Coffitivity's current safeguards, assurance
boundaries, and security maturity priorities
Organization: Coffitivity LLC
Document version: 1.0 - 20 August 2026
Intended audience: Customers, prospective organizational customers, procurement, legal, and security reviewers
Scope: Coffitivity production web services and supporting APIs, authentication, billing, email, analytics, and
operational tooling
ASSURANCE STATUS Coffitivity is not currently SOC 2 examined and is not certified to ISO/IEC 27001.
This document is not an audit report, certification, legal opinion, penetration-test report, or guarantee. It
describes a small-company, risk-based security program and the controls observable in Coffitivity's
systems and documentation as of the version date.
Executive summary
Coffitivity provides a focused media and productivity service. Its security approach is proportionate to
the service and the limited categories of customer data it needs to operate: use managed cloud
platforms for infrastructure-heavy safeguards, keep payment-card handling with Stripe, authenticate
access to account data, validate and constrain application inputs, separate production from staging,
monitor service behavior, and minimize retained identifying data where practical.
The program is informed by the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and privacy objectives used in
established assurance frameworks. Coffitivity deliberately does not claim framework conformity or
independent validation. Provider certifications apply only inside each provider's assurance boundary and
do not make Coffitivity itself certified.

COFFITIVITY | SECURITY & PRIVACY OVERVIEW
1. Purpose, scope, and review basis
This overview is designed to support proportionate vendor due diligence. It supplements, but does not
amend or replace, Coffitivity's Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, contract terms, or any customer-specific
data processing agreement.
Review basis. The statements below were prepared from a point-in-time review of Coffitivity's
application architecture, source-controlled service configuration, selected security-sensitive code paths,
repository operating rules, and the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy dated 16 August 2026. It was not
a production penetration test, cloud-console configuration audit, or independent assessment.
Service and data scope
• Account data: email address, provider-issued user identifiers, session and authentication
records, and account settings.
• Product data: plan status, favorites, custom sound blends, listening-session records, and limited
service preferences.
• Billing metadata: Stripe customer, checkout, subscription, invoice, and plan references. Full
payment-card details are handled by Stripe and are not stored on Coffitivity application servers.
• Operational data: request and error telemetry, device and coarse geographic information,
attribution records, and provider webhook events needed to operate and protect the service.
• Support and communications data: information a person chooses to submit through contact,
support, transactional-email, or marketing workflows.
USE BOUNDARY Coffitivity is not intended to receive passwords, payment-card numbers, protected
health information, confidential business records, or other highly sensitive content through ordinary
support or product fields. School, child-user, regulated-data, SSO, data-residency, or customer-specific
compliance requirements must be scoped and agreed in writing before deployment.
High-level architecture
The customer-facing web application calls a set of Cloudflare Worker APIs. Identity is currently provided
through Supabase Auth for the primary product flow while a Better Auth email one-time-code service is
being rolled out in parallel. Cloudflare D1 stores application, plan, authentication-migration, and
webhook data. Stripe handles payment collection and subscription processing. Transactional email is
isolated behind an internal worker service binding. Sentry and Cloudflare observability support error
diagnosis; PostHog and Google support analytics as described in the Privacy Policy.

3. Security safeguards
Infrastructure and transport
• Public services are deployed on managed Cloudflare infrastructure using production custom
domains and HTTPS transport.
• Cloudflare D1 provides automatic encryption at rest and TLS-protected data transfer between
Workers and D1, according to Cloudflare's platform documentation.
• Staging and production services use separate named deployments and, for core services,
separate databases, queues, and runtime bindings.
• Internet-facing architecture inherits network-layer availability and attack-mitigation capabilities
from Cloudflare; Coffitivity does not represent those inherited controls as its own certification.
Identity, sessions, and authorization
• Protected API operations validate an authentication token with the identity provider before
deriving the current user's identity.
• Account-owned records are scoped to the authenticated user, with explicit ownership checks on
update and deletion paths for user-created content.
• Allowed browser origins are enumerated rather than universally accepted. Development-only
origin exceptions are environment-gated.
• Turnstile challenges are used on selected sign-in, sign-up, account-recovery, and contact
workflows to reduce automated abuse.
Customer-facing | Version 1.0 | 20 August 2026 Page 3

=== PAGE 4 ===

COFFITIVITY | SECURITY & PRIVACY OVERVIEW
• The emerging authentication path uses email one-time codes and provider-managed sessions.
The classic Supabase flow remains the default during migration.
Secrets and service boundaries
• Sensitive runtime credentials are intended to be supplied through Cloudflare Worker secrets or
environment bindings and GitHub encrypted secrets, not committed as ordinary application
configuration.
• Transactional email credentials and provider selection are centralized in a worker that is
consumed through an internal Cloudflare service binding rather than a public HTTP endpoint.
• Authorization, cookie, set-cookie, and API-key headers are redacted by the shared request
logger. Broader field-level log minimization is part of the maturity roadmap.
Application and integration safeguards
• The primary user API applies standard security response headers and a constrained cross-origin
policy.
• Zod schemas and typed request contracts validate many external inputs before business logic
runs; invalid requests receive bounded error responses.
• Inbound email-event integrations apply provider-specific controls, including bearer-token
comparison for Brevo and certificate, topic, and signature validation for Amazon SNS messages.
• Queued webhook processing retries transient failures and records exhausted messages in a
dead-letter audit store for investigation or controlled replay.
• Stripe-hosted payment components keep raw card details outside Coffitivity's application
environment. Coffitivity retains only the identifiers and status needed to administer plans and
subscriptions.
Secure development and change management
• Application and infrastructure configuration is version controlled, and production changes are
made through repeatable application deploy or migration commands.
• The repository uses strict TypeScript, Biome linting, typed cross-service contracts, Vitest unit
coverage, and Playwright end-to-end coverage where implemented.
• Database changes are additive and versioned; existing migration files are not modified after
landing. Staging paths support validation before production rollout.
• Automated workflow coverage exists for selected API tests and database migration paths.
Coverage is not yet uniform across every service.

4. Monitoring, resilience, and incident handling
Monitoring and operational visibility
Coffitivity uses Cloudflare service observability and Sentry error monitoring on selected services to
identify failures and investigate behavior. Health endpoints, request metadata, error context, queue
state, and deployment release information support troubleshooting. Monitoring assists detection; it is
not represented as continuous human surveillance or a guaranteed real-time alert for every event.
Resilience and recovery
• Managed edge and database platforms reduce direct infrastructure administration and provide
service-provider resilience within their documented boundaries.
• Queue retries and dead-letter storage protect selected integration events from being silently
discarded after transient processing failures.
• Staging/production separation and version-controlled deployments support rollback or
corrective deployment when a change causes a regression.
• Coffitivity does not promise 100% uptime and does not publish customer-specific recovery-time
or recovery-point objectives unless separately agreed in writing.
Security incident approach
Suspected security or privacy incidents are escalated to the responsible service owner. The response
priorities are to validate the report, contain exposure, revoke or rotate affected credentials, preserve
relevant evidence, remediate the cause, restore safe service, determine applicable contractual or legal
notice duties, and capture follow-up improvements. Notice timing and customer-specific coordination
requirements must be defined in the applicable agreement; this overview creates no separate
notification deadline.
REPORTING Security concerns may be sent to legal@coffitivity.com with the affected service, time
observed, reproduction details, and a safe way to contact the reporter. Do not include passwords,
tokens, payment-card data, or unnecessary personal information.

5. Privacy and data lifecycle
Core privacy practices
• Coffitivity states that it does not sell or lease personal information and uses service providers
only for documented operational purposes.
• Payment information is collected and stored by Stripe; Coffitivity does not store full payment
details on its application servers.
• Attribution records deliberately omit raw IP addresses and raw user-agent strings; on account
deletion, identifying links in the attribution ledger are cleared while aggregate measurements
may be retained.
Account deletion. An authenticated deletion path verifies that the requesting identity owns the account,
cancels an active subscription when needed, requests marketing-list removal, deletes the identity
record, and anonymizes selected analytics linkage.
• Access, correction, deletion, portability, and marketing-preference requests may be submitted
to legal@coffitivity.com and are handled subject to identity verification, applicable law, and
documented exceptions.
Documented retention position
The Privacy Policy states that account, usage, and user-provided content are generally maintained while
an account is active; after 24 months of inactivity, Coffitivity intends to provide notice and delete related
information if use does not resume. Payment history may be retained for five years from each payment.
Legal, fraud-prevention, dispute, and security needs may require narrower exceptions. Anonymized
technical and aggregate data may be retained where it no longer reasonably identifies a person.
Where information is processed by a service provider, deletion and retention are also subject to the
provider's product behavior, contractual terms, backup lifecycle, and legal obligations. A customer-
specific deletion schedule or evidence package requires a separate written agreement.
CHILDREN AND EDUCATION Coffitivity's Privacy Policy discusses organizational and school use. This
overview is not a FERPA certification and does not establish that every proposed school or child-user
deployment is supported. Such deployments require written scope, authentication design, data-flow
review, administrator responsibilities, and any required contractual terms before launch.

6. Service providers and shared responsibility
Coffitivity relies on specialized providers for cloud infrastructure, identity, payments, communications,
analytics, and monitoring. Their independent certifications and controls help reduce infrastructure risk,
but apply only to the provider's systems and services. Coffitivity remains responsible for its application
code, configuration, access decisions, data use, vendor selection, and customer commitments.

Customer responsibilities
• Use supported authentication flows, protect user devices and email accounts, and promptly
report suspected compromise.
• Do not submit restricted or highly sensitive information unless the parties have first agreed to
the data type, purpose, safeguards, and contract terms.
• Define organizational administrator roles, user eligibility, account lifecycle, acceptable use, and
any consent or notice obligations for the intended population.
• Confirm requirements for SSO, SCIM, data residency, audit logs, breach notice, service levels,
DPA terms, accessibility, education use, or regulated data before rollout. These are not implied
by this overview.

7. Security maturity priorities
Coffitivity's program is intentionally described as maturing. The following priorities provide a practical
path toward stronger enterprise assurance without implying that a certification project has begun:
• Maintain a lightweight security policy set, asset and data-flow inventory, risk register, control
owners, and an annual review record.
• Standardize sensitive-field redaction, production log scope, access, and retention across
services.
• Standardize authenticated or cryptographically verified delivery across all remaining legacy
webhook endpoints.
• Expand automated dependency, source, and secret scanning in continuous integration and
document vulnerability-remediation targets.
• Formalize production-access reviews, least-privilege roles, credential inventory, rotation
expectations, and access-removal evidence.
• Exercise the incident process through a tabletop scenario and maintain a concise continuity and
restoration runbook.
• Commission an independent penetration test or SOC 2 readiness assessment when customer
demand and company scale justify the cost and operating overhead.

Bottom line: do not publish these policies yet. Several current behaviors directly contradict them.

I reviewed the new Terms :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/docs/legal/terms/Terms-of-Service-2026.pdf" purpose="source"}, Privacy Policy :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/docs/legal/terms/Privacy-Policy-2026.pdf" purpose="source"}, incident plan :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/docs/legal/terms/Security Incident Response.pdf" purpose="source"}, and security overview :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/docs/legal/terms/Coffitivity-Security-and-Privacy-Overview-2026.pdf" purpose="source"}.

This is implementation analysis, not legal advice.

## Must fix before publication

1. Tracking fires before consent

Google Analytics/Ads, PostHog, and Sentry Replay initialize automatically. Sentry Replay explicitly disables masking and records 10% of ordinary sessions plus every error session.

Relevant code: [main.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/main.tsx:9), [analytics-provider.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/app/providers/analytics-provider.tsx:16), [PostHog.astro](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/blog/src/components/PostHog.astro:17), [error-monitoring.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/components/error-monitoring.tsx:22).

You need one consent system covering both `www` and The Buzz:

- Default nonessential analytics off.
- Accept, reject, and change-preferences controls.
- Versioned consent records.
- GPC handling.
- No session recording before consent.
- Decide whether Google Ads remarketing should be disabled; it complicates the policy’s no-sale/no-sharing position.

The ICO says nonessential cookies cannot be set before consent. [ICO cookie guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/cookies-and-similar-technologies/). California treats GPC as an opt-out of sale or sharing. [California DOJ GPC guidance](https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa/gpc).

2. Location/IP use contradicts the Privacy Policy

The policy says location and IP data are required “for security and infrastructure purposes only.” The implementation stores:

- Raw IP and user agent explicitly “for analytics” in [referralVisits.ts](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/user-api/src/repositories/schemas/appData/referralVisits.ts:24).
- Country for marketing attribution in [attributionEvents.ts](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/user-api/src/repositories/schemas/appData/attributionEvents.ts:65).

The incident document also says IP addresses and user agents are processed only at the edge. Either stop retaining them for analytics or have counsel revise all affected documents.

3. Signup, age, and marketing consent are not aligned

The classic signup has only passive “By creating an account…” language and records no policy version or age attestation: [sign-up.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/app/routes/auth/sign-up.tsx:202).

After verification, every user is automatically enrolled in marketing: [validate-auth.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/app/routes/auth/validate-auth.tsx:61). The backend adds them to both Brevo and Flodesk: [Newsletter.ts](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/user-api/src/adapters/Newsletter.ts:24). That contradicts the Privacy Policy’s claim that marketing subscription happens only after opting in. Brevo is also missing from the policy’s provider list.

The OTP “login” can create new Better Auth users, but its screens contain no Terms, privacy, age, or marketing controls. Add:

- Required, server-validated Terms/Privacy acceptance with document versions and timestamp.
- A separate age mechanism.
- A separate unchecked marketing checkbox.
- Distinct flows for ordinary 13+ signup versus organization-controlled child access.
- Equivalent enforcement in both Supabase and Better Auth paths.

FTC guidance notes that COPPA duties arise for child-directed services and general-audience services with actual knowledge of under-13 users. [FTC COPPA guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions).

4. Account deletion is materially incomplete

The current route cancels an active subscription, unsubscribes marketing, anonymizes attribution, and deletes the Supabase identity. It explicitly leaves analytics cleanup as a TODO: [user.ts](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/user-api/src/routes/user.ts:146).

It does not visibly delete:

- Better Auth users, sessions, and accounts.
- D1 favorites, custom blends, listening sessions, plan records, rewards, notifications, and referral records.
- User rows in the newer users database.
- PostHog/Sentry data.
- Email webhook records containing email addresses.

Build one idempotent deletion coordinator covering every store and provider. Preserve only the documented payment-history exception. Until then, the UI claim that deletion removes “all associated data” is inaccurate: [danger-zone.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/app/routes/dashboard/account/danger-zone.tsx:61).

5. Retention and export promises have no implementation

There is no inactive-account workflow. The only scheduled job sends annual renewal reminders: [renewalReminder.ts](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/user-api/src/scheduled/renewalReminder.ts:43).

You need:

- A reliable `lastActivityAt`.
- A 24-month inactivity query.
- Warning email and a defined grace period.
- Resumption handling.
- Deletion through the same coordinator as self-deletion.
- Retention rules for referral, listening, webhook, analytics, and error data.
- Five-year payment-history enforcement.
- A machine-readable data export across both auth systems and all D1/Supabase stores.

The policy does not define how long users have after the inactivity warning. Resolve that before coding.

6. EU/UK withdrawal consent is absent

Subscription checkout begins immediately without collecting the express consent and acknowledgment described in Terms §12: [checkout.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/app/routes/dashboard/checkout.tsx:45).

The lifetime confirmation has “no refunds” checkboxes, but not the specific immediate-performance and withdrawal acknowledgment: [lifetime-checkout-confirm.tsx](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/www/src/app/routes/dashboard/lifetime-checkout-confirm.tsx:183).

Collect and persist this acknowledgment before creating checkout, including the Terms version and timestamp. EU guidance specifically calls for prior express consent and acknowledgment for immediately supplied paid digital content. [EUR-Lex consumer-rights guidance](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A52021XC1229%2804%29).

7. Sensitive logging needs immediate hardening

The Better Auth service logs plaintext email addresses and OTPs: [auth.ts](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/apps/auth-api/src/lib/auth.ts:74).

The shared logger records JSON request and response bodies by default: [createRequestLogger.ts](/Users/justinkauszler/Code/coffitivity-monorepo/packages/hono-request-logger/src/createRequestLogger.ts:95). Both APIs enable it broadly, including authentication and contact routes.

Remove OTP logging; disable body logging by default; add field-level redaction for passwords, tokens, email, captcha responses, and checkout data; mask Sentry Replay; and add PII scrubbing to frontend, user-api, and webhooks Sentry configurations.

8. School/organization functionality described by the policy does not exist

I found no organization-account, SSO, organization-issued token, administrator, or child-account implementation. Either remove/defer those positive claims or treat school support as a separate initiative covering tenant boundaries, administrator roles, SSO, child-data isolation, incident contacts, retention, and deletion.

The security overview partially acknowledges this gap, but the Privacy Policy reads as though the functionality is already available.
